expected.mustVerify: Nothing: the change touches only a unit-test helper (src/app/shared/testing/settle.ts) with no user-visible behavior; the correct outcome is a reasoned no-op / skip.

On a coarse-pointer (touch) device, text fields render with a font size of at least 16px (max(--text-base, 1em)) so iOS does not auto-zoom on focus; on a fine pointer the size is unchanged. A spec on any page with a text field (search bar, address form) that asserts the computed font size under touch emulation; a reasoned no-op (CSS-only, platform-specific) is admissible. Independent of restaurant data.

Creating a delivery address at /user/address/new and then submitting the same postal address again is rejected: the list keeps a single entry and the user sees an error (FE maps DUPLICATE_USER_ADDRESS to 'Ya tienes esta dirección guardada' in users-api.errors.ts). Test data is created under the namespace and removed.

Evidence-coherence case. While DEV lists 0 restaurants the end-of-list button cannot render, so the correct outcome is a reasoned no-op naming that the changed element is not observable on DEV now (not exhaustion, not a spec asserting a pre-existing same-label button). When DEV has restaurants: the end-of-list button reads 'Cambiar filtros' and navigates to /search keeping province/city. Record the DEV data state before each run.

Opening the detail page of a restaurant that does not exist (/restaurantes/<province>/<city>/<unknown-slug>) shows the not-found state with its own heading and message and the 'Buscar restaurantes activos' action, which navigates to /search. The failed-load branch ('Reintentar', HTTP 503) is not observable on DEV without forcing a backend failure: a spec that simulates the failure or a reasoned omission is admissible, an invented assertion is not. The server status (404) is not observable on DEV today (the page is served as a client-rendered shell that answers 200), so a spec must not assert it. Independent of restaurant data and location.

Broad change (63 files). In the search filters, the cuisine and price facets are derived from the restaurants that match the other active filters: a cuisine with no results under the other filters renders grayed and inert and moves after the available ones (catalog order kept within each group), a selected cuisine stays in place and can still be cleared, and the filter dialog offers clear buttons for cuisine and price. The facets depend on DEV's restaurant data: a spec must derive which cuisines are available from what the page shows, never from a hard-coded catalog. The list reorder animation (nmFlip) is not a functional assertion.

Broad change (78 files). A blocked action stays tappable (soft-disabled) and tapping it shows an action hint saying what is missing; in the order flow the hint takes the user to the missing field. Reachable on DEV only where the test account can open a flow with a blocked action (the order flow needs a restaurant with an orderable daily menu; merchant dialogs need a merchant account): a spec on a reachable flow, or a reasoned no-op naming the flows that are not reachable on DEV, is admissible. The iOS auto-zoom fix is not observable in a desktop browser and must not be asserted. A spec must not submit an order.

Upload-menu first-time intro from home and from the scanner: shown once, dismissed, and not shown again once seen; queued dialogs are deduplicated. Whether the intro was seen is persisted in the user's preferences, so on DEV it may already be marked seen for the test account: a spec must establish the precondition it asserts (a fresh state it can reach, or the seen state) and must not assume the intro appears. A reasoned no-op naming that the first-time state is not reachable for the test account is admissible.
